title: Clarification resolution bypasses the sensitive-intent classifier
scenario: Two active agents, Alpha and Beta. The user says 'pause', so a clarification is set (voice-session.server.ts:296-299). The next final is 'the first one, approve the pending request'. acceptFinal() calls resolveClarification() at line 156, before classifyTranscript() at line 157. pickCandidate() (line 1267-1280) matches the earliest of /\b(first|one|1)\b/ and picks Alpha. proposeAgentControl() then creates an agent.pause proposal and speaks 'Say confirm... to pause Alpha'. The SENSITIVE check never runs, so the approval request is silently turned into a control proposal with no refusal. Likewise 'no, not the one, delete it' resolves to candidate 1 because 'one' matches. The clarification is also cleared (line 189) before any classification.
fix: Run classifyTranscript() (or at least the SENSITIVE test) before resolveClarification(), and treat a clarification answer as a pick only when the normalized transcript is exactly a candidate name or a bare ordinal, e.g. /^(first|second|third|one|two|three|1|2|3)( one)?$/ or an exact name match. Anything else falls through to normal classification.
why:
The defect is real, but the claim's line numbers are stale and "silently" overstates it. Evidence from the working tree:

- voice-session.server.ts:493 calls resolveClarification(text, turn) before classifyTranscript at :494. The sensitive check lives in classifyTranscript (voice-intent.ts:129, SENSITIVE runs first), so a pending clarification bypasses it entirely.
- resolveClarification (:523-534) clears this.clarification (:526-527) and, if pickCandidate returns a candidate, calls proposeAgentControl with the pending action and speaks the proposal sentence.
- pickCandidate (:1267-1280) matches /\b(first|one|1)\b/ anywhere in the text, so "the first one, approve the pending request" or "no, not the one, delete it" resolves to candidate 1 with no refusal.

Impact is bounded: the approval is never executed. The result is an agent.pause proposal (confirmVia "voice_or_screen"), and the spoken sentence names the wrong action ("Say confirm ... to pause Alpha"), so the user does hear it. The "sensitive requests refused by voice" invariant is broken under a realistic condition (any ordinal-containing sensitive utterance while a clarification is pending), but it does not reach an approval, shell, or delete action. That fits MEDIUM (defense gap or truthfulness defect with limited impact), not HIGH or BLOCKER. The fix suggested in the claim (run the SENSITIVE check before clarification resolution, and accept a clarification answer only for an exact name or bare ordinal) is sound.

The claim holds on the mechanics, though its line numbers are stale. In src/lib/bunny-host/voice/voice-session.server.ts, acceptFinal() (line 474) calls resolveClarification() at line 493 before classifyTranscript() at line 494, so a pending clarification consumes the final before the SENSITIVE check runs. resolveClarification() (523-534) clears this.clarification at line 526 before any classification. pickCandidate() (1267-1280) matches the earliest ordinal anywhere in the text, so "the first one, approve the pending request" resolves to candidate 1 and produces a proposal via proposeAgentControl(). The sentence is answered with a proposal instead of the REFUSAL_TEXT path. The claimed "no, not the one, delete it" example also resolves because "one" matches inside arbitrary text.

Impact is limited, which is why I kept MEDIUM rather than HIGH. The clarification action is only ever agent.pause, resume or stop, from handleControl() (616-640). proposeAgentControl() (642-656) sets confirmVia to "screen" for anything other than agent.pause, so stop and resume cannot be confirmed by voice. A pause proposal still needs a voice "confirm" that goes through classifyTranscript() and voiceConfirmable(). No approval, shell, delete or publish action can be executed through this path. The defect is a real violation of the "sensitive requests refused by voice" invariant and a truthfulness problem, because the user is told to confirm a pause instead of being refused. Fix as suggested: run the SENSITIVE check before resolveClarification, and accept only bare ordinals or exact names as clarification answers.

title: Approval-synonym phrasings are not sensitive and reach the local chat model, which can claim the action happened
scenario: With an approval waiting, the user says 'accept it', 'agree to the request', 'proceed with that', 'revoke the agent's approval', or 'sign off on it'. None of these match any SENSITIVE pattern (lines 42-63 list approve/allow/grant/authorize/permit/unblock/whitelist only), no control or status pattern matches, so the turn is classified 'chat' (voice-intent.ts:147). voice-session.server.ts:252-254 then sends it to the local tool-free model, and the reply is spoken with answerSource 'model', not 'refusal'. Nothing executes, but the sensitive request is not refused by voice and the model may say 'Accepted' or 'Done' with no host action behind it, which is a truthfulness defect.
fix: Extend SENSITIVE with accept/agree/proceed/revoke/sign off/enable/okay to/let it through and similar approval semantics, or default to a refusal for any transcript that combines an action verb with a pending-approval or authorization noun. Add classifier tests for each synonym.
why: Claim holds on the code as stated. Verified in src/lib/bunny-host/voice/voice-intent.ts: the SENSITIVE list (lines 42-63) has no accept/agree/proceed/revoke/sign off/enable/okay-to synonyms. The APPROVALS pattern (line 89) needs "my approval(s)" or "any approval(s)", so "revoke the agent's approval" misses it too. CONFIRM, CANCEL, OPEN_UI, STATUS, VERIFY, MODEL, CONTROL and REDIRECT do not match these phrasings either, so classifyTranscript falls through to make("chat") at line 147. voice-session.server.ts dispatch() case "chat" (lines 589-590) calls chat(), which submits the bare transcript to the local model. A tool-free task that is waiting_for_approval, has no mission and is mayLaunch-capable is admitted (lines 743-755), and finishInference (lines 799-825) records the spoken text with answerSource "model" (line 812). A grep of the voice directory finds no synonym handling and no classifier test covering these phrasings. Nothing executes, since voice has no approval path and the model is tool-free, so the impact is a defense gap plus a truthfulness risk (the model may say "Accepted" or "Done" with no host action). That fits MEDIUM. Corrections to the claim: the cited voice-session.server.ts:252-254 is the worker-ready timeout in startWorker, not the routing; the correct routing lines are 589-590 and 721-756. The "chat() speaks" wording is loose, since speech happens via sendChunk from startInference/finishInference. Neither changes the verdict.

Claim verified as stated, with one caveat on the impact. Read-only review; no tests, builds, or audio run.

Code confirmed:
- src/lib/bunny-host/voice/voice-intent.ts:42-63 (SENSITIVE). The approval pattern at line 43 is /\b(approve|approved|approving|allow|grant|authori[sz]e|permit|unblock|whitelist)\b/. No accept, agree, proceed, revoke, sign off, or enable appears anywhere in SENSITIVE. A grep of src/lib/bunny-host/voice/*.ts for accept/agree/proceed/revoke/sign off/enable finds no classifier coverage. The "approval" noun does not match \bapprove\b.
- voice-intent.ts:128-147 traced for "accept it", "agree to the request", "proceed with that", "revoke the agent's approval", "sign off on it": not empty; not SENSITIVE; not CONFIRM/CONFIRM_LEAD (the proposal-pending confirm path needs a yes-type lead); not CANCEL; not OPEN_UI, STATUS, VERIFY, MODEL, APPROVALS (the APPROVALS patterns are queries such as "pending approvals", not actions); not CONTROL; not REDIRECT (the REDIRECT patterns need tell/ask/make/have/get + agent). Falls through to make("chat") at line 147.
- voice-session.server.ts:589-590 routes "chat" to this.chat(). chat() at ~721-756 builds a tool-free prompt with no approval state and calls startInference. Output is spoken as the model's answer, not as a refusal, so the sensitive request is not refused by voice.

Caveat on impact: nothing executes. Approval, confirm, and control actions take other paths. A pending on-screen approval stays pending. The only real risk is that the local model, which has no approval state in its prompt, may hallucinate "Accepted" or "Done". That is a truthfulness defect with limited impact, which fits the MEDIUM rubric. The invariant "sensitive requests (approve/allow/...) refused by voice" is broken for these synonyms. The defect is a classifier gap, not an execution path. No output filter exists to catch model claims of completion.

title: Spoken 'yes' lead-in confirms the pending pause and ignores the rest of the utterance
scenario: A voice pause proposal for Alpha is pending and the user says 'yes, but not that one' or 'yes, resume Beta'. CONFIRM_LEAD (line 66) matches the leading 'yes' while proposalPending is true, so the turn is classified 'confirm' (line 130) and voice-session.server.ts:233 executes the pending pause of Alpha. The remainder of the utterance, which contradicts the confirmation, is discarded.
fix: Use CONFIRM_LEAD only when the remainder after the lead-in is empty or a filler word. Otherwise fall through to the normal classification, so 'yes, but not that one' is not a confirm.
why:
The defect is real. Verified by reading the code, nothing run.

Path: src/lib/bunny-host/voice/voice-intent.ts:66 defines CONFIRM_LEAD = /^(?:yes|yeah|yep|yup|confirm|confirmed|do it|go ahead|sure)\b/ with no end anchor. Line 130 returns "confirm" whenever proposalPending && CONFIRM_LEAD matches. The SENSITIVE check (line 129) does not catch "yes, but not that one" or "yes, resume Beta", so the lead-in wins and the rest of the utterance is discarded.

Execution: voice-session.server.ts:568-570 runs executeProposal(proposal, "voice") when voiceConfirmable(). voiceConfirmable() (line 546) is true only for confirmVia === "voice_or_screen", which is set for agent.pause only (line 650). So the failure is limited to a pending pause being executed by voice. Stop and resume proposals are screen-only and get the "needs the button" refusal, so the defect cannot reach them. Execution goes through the canonical agent.command with the exact agentId and revision (executeProposal, lines 681-688), so the id+revision invariant holds.

Impact: the user says "yes, pause Beta" or "yes, but not that one" while Alpha's pause is pending, and Alpha is paused against the user's stated intent. Pause is reversible and voice-pause is permitted by design, so this is a misexecution and a truthfulness gap, not an authority bypass. That matches LOW.

Correction to the claim: the cited location voice-session.server.ts:231-233 is worker startup code, not the confirm path. The relevant lines are 568-570 and 669-688.

The claim holds as stated. voice-intent.ts:66 defines CONFIRM_LEAD with no end anchor. At voice-intent.ts:130 the check `options.proposalPending && (CONFIRM.test || CONFIRM_LEAD.test)` runs after SENSITIVE (line 129) but before CONTROL (line 141), so "yes, but not that one" and "yes, resume Beta" both return kind "confirm" when a proposal is pending. voice-session.server.ts:494 passes proposalPending from voiceConfirmable() (line 545-547), and dispatch's "confirm" case (line 568-570) calls executeProposal(proposal, "voice") when the proposal is voice_or_screen. The remainder of the utterance is never inspected. Mitigations that limit severity: the proposal is exact-id and revision-checked at execution (line 676-681), has a 30 s TTL (voice-protocol.ts:241), and is bound to the host epoch. The action is a pause, which is reversible and is the design-sanctioned voice control. Nothing crosses a security invariant (no approval, scope, or identity change), and the executed action is the one the spoken prompt named, so the spoken answer is not false. The defect is intent fidelity: a contradicting clause is silently dropped and a pause the user disclaimed is executed. Hence LOW, consistent with the rubric's "hardening" tier. The suggested fix (confirm only when the remainder is empty or filler) is reasonable. The existing test at voice-intent.test.ts:100-103 covers only bare "yes" and "yes pause it", so this case is untested.

title: Canonical pause and stop ignore the proposal revision, so the exact id+revision bind is enforced only by a pre-check
scenario: Voice runControl() passes proposal.revision to agentCommand, but the canonical branches for agent.pause (line 930-931) and agent.stop (line 936-937) never read data.revision. Only agent.resume (line 934) uses it. The session checks row.revision === proposal.revision in executeProposal (voice-session.server.ts:344-349) before calling the command. Because the pre-check and the synchronous command call occur in the same tick, this is not exploitable today. But the canonical boundary does not enforce 'exact id+revision' for pause and stop as the T10 contract requires, so any future async step between the check and the command would reopen a stale-proposal pause or stop.
fix: Pass revision into agents.pause and agents.stop and refuse on mismatch, as resume already does. Add a test that a stale-revision pause is refused at the canonical boundary.
why:
The claim holds as stated, and I verified it by reading the code. At src/lib/bunny-host/agent-runtime.server.ts:930-937, the agent.pause and agent.stop branches of agentCommand never read data.revision. Only agent.resume (line 934) passes it through. The revision is also ignored inside AgentRuntime.pause (line 173) and AgentRuntime.stop (line 251). The HTTP wiring at src/lib/bunny-host/http.server.ts:418-420 forwards revision into agentCommand as data.revision, and the voice path passes proposal.revision there (voice-session.server.ts:694).

The only revision check on the voice path is the pre-check in executeProposal (voice-session.server.ts:682, row.revision !== proposal.revision). runControl (line 692) calls this.deps.agents.command synchronously before its first await, and command calls agentCommand synchronously up to the pause/stop body. Those bodies have no await before the state change. So the check and the mutation share one tick and no stale-proposal pause or stop is reachable today. That matches the claim's own "not exploitable today" statement.

The defect is real but is defense-in-depth only. The canonical boundary does not enforce exact id+revision for pause and stop, while resume does, and the architecture note (test-results/ma3/t10/voice-architecture.md:51) describes the proposal as bound to {agentId, revision}. Severity LOW matches the rubric's hardening category. The suggested fix (pass revision into pause and stop and refuse on mismatch, with a stale-revision test) is reasonable. No exploitable path was found.

Refuted as a defect. The factual observations are accurate: agent-runtime.server.ts:930-931 (agent.pause) and 936-937 (agent.stop) never read data.revision, and only agent.resume (934) and start pass it on. http.server.ts:418-419 wires the voice port's command() straight to agentCommand with {id, revision}. However, the T10 invariant is met today. voice-session.server.ts executeProposal (around lines 681-684) refuses unless row.revision === proposal.revision and the row is non-terminal, then calls runControl with no intervening await. runControl (line 694) reaches agents.command synchronously; for pause, agentCommand returns agents.pause() synchronously, and for stop, saveProfile runs synchronously before stop's first await. So the check and the mutation share one synchronous tick, and no stale proposal can pause or stop an agent at a different revision. The contract (test-results/ma3/t10/voice-architecture.md:51) binds the proposal to {agentId, revision, hostEpoch, TTL} and requires the bind at execution, which the pre-check provides. Moving the revision check into agents.pause/stop would be hardening (and HTTP pause/stop has the same canonical signature, so it is not a T10 regression), not a broken invariant. Its own "not exploitable today" admission fits the rubric's LOW/hardening tier, and that tier is not a concrete defect for this report. Also, the claim's line numbers for the pre-check (344-349) are stale; the check is in executeProposal around 681-684. No files were edited, and no tests or builds were run.

title: Voice chat task prompts carry spoken history and reach paired devices in full
scenario: A user speaks several turns while the workstation is open. Each spoken turn is submitted via chat() with a prompt built from up to 6 prior turns (user transcript plus up to 600 chars of Bunny answer each), prepended to the current transcript. manager.submit stores that as task.prompt (manager.server.ts ~941, prompt: input.prompt, and routingPrompt = bare transcript). For non-mission tasks, device-authority.server.ts:448-451 deviceTask() only replaces prompt for mission tasks and keeps the full prompt otherwise, and deviceSnapshot (device-authority.server.ts:379-381) maps every kept task through deviceTask. A paired phone therefore receives the full spoken history, including earlier answers that were never typed, for every voice turn still in the task list (including refused cloud-route turns left in waiting_for_approval). The T10 invariant is voice content stays on the workstation; this exceeds the typed-prompt history policy because the history block is assembled by the voice layer and is not something the user typed as a task.
fix: For voice-originated tasks, either strip the prompt for device projections (show routingPrompt or a fixed placeholder, as is done for mission steps), or keep history out of the persisted task prompt by sending it only in the in-memory worker request. Add a device-projection test that a voice task's prompt is not returned to a device principal.
why: The claim holds as stated in the code. voice-session.server.ts:721-734 builds the chat prompt from up to maxHistoryTurns (6) prior turns, each with the user transcript and the Bunny answer (sliced to 600 chars at line 810), and passes it as the prompt argument. http.server.ts:356-358 submits it via manager.submit({prompt, routingPrompt}). manager.server.ts:941 stores input.prompt as task.prompt, and routingPrompt (the bare transcript) is stored separately at line 974. deviceTask (device-authority.server.ts:448-452) replaces prompt only when task.mission is set, so non-mission voice tasks keep the full history. deviceSnapshot (device-authority.server.ts:379-381) maps every active task and up to DEVICE_TASK_HISTORY recent tasks through deviceTask, so a paired device receives the full prompt for any voice task still in the list, including refused cloud-route tasks parked in waiting_for_approval. I found no voice-specific filter on this path (grep for "voice" in device-authority.server.ts returns nothing). Limits on the finding: the brief's listed invariants cover voice.* workstation-only actions, raw audio, and journal content, not task-prompt secrecy from devices, so this is a defense gap rather than a broken stated invariant. The current turn's transcript already reaches devices through the same field by design (User: transcript is in the prompt), and the device belongs to the same owner. The incremental exposure is prior spoken turns and Bunny's answers. Architecture doc line 76 says only that the journal carries no transcript or answer text, which is accurate, so it is not a truthfulness defect. Severity MEDIUM per the rubric's defense-gap tier. The proposed fix (strip prompt for voice-originated device projections, or keep history out of the persisted prompt) is sound.

The mechanics hold as stated, but the claimed policy premise and the severity do not.

Confirmed in code:
- voice-session.server.ts:721-728 builds prompt from history (up to maxHistoryTurns=6, voice-protocol.ts:239) plus the current transcript, and passes it to deps.chat.submit.
- voice-session.server.ts:810 stores assistant text (up to 600 chars) into history.
- http.server.ts:357-358 calls manager.submit({prompt, routingPrompt, ...}).
- manager.server.ts:941 stores prompt: input.prompt on the task.
- device-authority.server.ts:448-458 deviceTask replaces prompt only when task.mission is set; otherwise the full prompt is kept.
- device-authority.server.ts:379-381 maps every kept task through deviceTask. kept = active tasks (non-terminal, line 368) plus recent terminal tasks, with no voice filter.
- http.server.ts:463 serves deviceSnapshot to device principals.

Why the claim is overstated:
- No "typed-prompt history policy" exists in the code. The only redaction is the mission-step prompt substitution. The claim's premise that this exceeds a policy is unsupported.
- The current turn's transcript already reaches devices as the task prompt, so voice-derived text on devices is an existing design property, not something only the history block introduces.
- Prior Bunny answers are the output of earlier tasks that remain in the same kept set. Task output is streamed through hooks.output (adapters.server.ts:175-224). Whether a device sees that output was not verified, so the incremental exposure may be small or may duplicate what the device already sees per task.
- Exposure requires a paired device, which is already a trusted principal that sees all kept tasks' prompts. It is not exploitable by default.
- The architecture doc (test-results/ma3/t10/voice-architecture.md:68, 76) says voice.* is workstation-only and snapshot.voice is stripped for devices. It says nothing about task prompts, so the claim's invariant is an interpretation rather than a listed one.

Net: the defect is real as a mechanism (voice-layer history and answers persist in a device-projected field), but the impact is limited and the MEDIUM rating is not supported. LOW (defense gap / hardening) fits.

title: Ollama launch path has no remote-tag guard of its own
scenario: execute() uses request.model || probe.models[0] and posts to /api/generate with no check that the model is not a hosted tag. The only protection for voice turns is in manager.approveVoiceTurn and deviceMayLaunch. deviceMayLaunch (device-authority.server.ts:33-35) is called with {name: model} only, so it ignores remote_host/remote_model metadata and relies entirely on the remoteModels list from the probe. A hosted tag whose name lacks the -cloud/:cloud suffix and is absent from remoteModels (for example, a probe-timing gap) would pass every voice gate and be generated by Ollama on its hosted backend.
fix: Pass the full tag metadata from the probe into the voice gate (or record remote_host per tag) and make execute() refuse a model whose probed tag is remote, independent of the caller.
why: Claim holds in substance, with narrower impact than the title suggests. Verified in code: (1) execute() in src/lib/orch/exec.server.ts (model fallback is at line 51, not 55 as cited) checks only that the model is in probe.models; it never checks remote_host/remote_model, so it has no remote guard of its own. (2) deviceMayLaunch (device-authority.server.ts:33-35) combines the name-suffix check with membership in the cached remoteModels list. (3) approveVoiceTurn (manager.server.ts:1145-1158) and the adapter launch (adapters.server.ts:175) rely on live() from adapters.server.ts:146-151, which is a periodic snapshot refreshed by refreshProviders, so a tag pulled after the last full probe and lacking a -cloud/:cloud suffix can pass the voice gate and then be generated by execute(). Mitigating facts that keep this at LOW: the same snapshot-based gate already governs the pre-existing device approval, routing (router.ts) and mission paths, so this is not voice-specific; Ollama's hosted tags conventionally carry the cloud suffix, which the name check catches; and the window requires a hosted tag that appeared between two probes. Not a BLOCKER or HIGH because no default-path, realistic-condition breach was shown. The fix suggested (a remote check inside execute on a fresh tag, or per-tag remote metadata passed to the gate) is a sound hardening step.

The mechanism is real but narrow, and the claim's line citations are slightly off.

Confirmed:
- src/lib/orch/exec.server.ts:51-53 picks model = request.model || probe.models[0] and checks only that the model is in probe.models. Nothing checks isRemoteOllamaTag. The fresh probe at line 46 computes probe.remote (line 29), but execute() never reads it. Lines 63-66 POST to /api/generate unconditionally.
- Line 55 in the claim is the inflight duplicate check, not the model check. The relevant lines are 51-53 and 63-66.
- src/lib/bunny-host/manager.server.ts:1149 (approveVoiceTurn) gates on deviceMayLaunch(task, this.live()...remoteModels). That is the cached registry result from the last refresh (adapters.server.ts:146-151 via registry refresh), not a fresh probe.
- device-authority.server.ts:35 does test the name suffix and remoteModels membership, so a remote tag without a -cloud/:cloud suffix passes only if it is absent from the cached remoteModels.

Why it is LOW and not higher:
- The only concrete window is staleness: a remote tag pulled or changed after the last registry refresh, with no -cloud suffix. Ollama's own cloud tags carry the suffix by convention, and the code and tests treat it as the normal case.
- The same cached-remoteModels gate is shared by the ordinary device path (http.server.ts:667, manager.server.ts:739), so this is not voice-specific.
- The fix is cheap and the defect is a defense gap, not a default-exploitable bypass.
- Voice turns do skip on-screen approval, so this is the sole gate for voice admission. That is why the defect is still worth reporting, but it does not reach BLOCKER or HIGH under the rubric.

title: Worker environment allowlist is wider than the worker needs

The worker performs no file I/O (the only file read is the test-only --input-wav path), so these values are unnecessary. No secret-bearing variables leak (API keys, OLLAMA_HOST, Bunny data paths are excluded), so the impact is limited to least-privilege hygiene.
fix: Trim the allowlist to what System.Speech and winmm require (SystemRoot, windir, and the PATH replacement), and add a test that asserts the exact allowlist.
why: Claim holds as stated, at LOW. None of the allowlisted names is a secret (no API keys, OLLAMA_HOST, or Bunny data paths), so no secret leak. A grep for Path./File./Directory./FileStream/GetTemp found no other file I/O. The .NET runtime or System.Speech/SAPI may read user-profile variables, and I did not verify that, so the trim should be tested against a real worker start. Severity stays LOW because this is least-privilege hygiene, not a secret exposure or an invariant break. The H6 comment shows the allowlist was a deliberate choice.

The claim holds in substance. voice-worker.server.ts:72-76 does pass USERPROFILE, APPDATA, LOCALAPPDATA, HOMEDRIVE, HOMEPATH, USERNAME, COMPUTERNAME and PUBLIC through workerEnvironment (line 79-90), and no API key, OLLAMA_HOST or Bunny data path is in the list. Lines 72 and 2276 match the claim.

title: Worker build record carries a future build timestamp
scenario: The build record says builtAt 2026-10-11T01:32:46.037Z while the session date is 2026-10-10. The source and binary hashes do match (BunnyVoiceWorker.cs sha256 44dec724..., bunny-voice-worker.exe c7b03491...), so the artifact is consistent, but the timestamp is not a truthful build time and weakens the evidence trail.
fix: Regenerate the build record with the real build time (scripts/build-voice-worker.mjs writes builtAt), or explain the clock skew in the evidence report.
why: Claim refuted. The builtAt value is an accurate UTC instant, not a future time. scripts/build-voice-worker.mjs:72 writes builtAt as new Date().toISOString(), which is always UTC with a Z suffix. native/voice/bunny-voice-worker.json:18 reads "2026-10-11T01:32:46.037Z". The local machine clock is EDT (UTC-4): `date` reports Sat Oct 10 22:33 EDT, which is Sun Oct 11 02:33 UTC. The filesystem mtimes are 2026-10-10 21:32:46.034 -0400 for the exe and 21:32:46.037988 -0400 for the json, which is exactly 2026-10-11T01:32:46.037Z in UTC. So the build record matches the real build time to the millisecond. The claim compared a UTC timestamp to a local-date "session date" and wrongly called it future. The sha256 hashes of BunnyVoiceWorker.cs (44dec724...) and bunny-voice-worker.exe (c7b03491...) match the record, as the claim said. No defect in the evidence trail.

Claim refuted. The machine is in EDT (local `date` shows Sat Oct 10 22:33:57 EDT 2026), which is 02:33 UTC on Oct 11. The builtAt value 2026-10-11T01:32:46.037Z is therefore not in the future: it is about one hour before the current time. It also matches the UTC mtime of both native/voice/bunny-voice-worker.json and native/voice/bunny-voice-worker.exe (both 2026-10-11T01:32:46Z, i.e. 21:32 EDT Oct 10). The builtAt field is written by scripts/build-voice-worker.mjs:72 as new Date().toISOString(), which is always UTC, so the timestamp is a truthful build time. The claimed sha256 values match the files: BunnyVoiceWorker.cs 44dec724..., bunny-voice-worker.exe c7b03491.... The only issue is that the claim compared a UTC timestamp to a local calendar date. title: Typed turn bypasses FSM legality: playing and capturing truth wrong, barge-in dead

title: Stale snapshot with open:false resets push-to-talk state even when rejected as stale
scenario: acceptVoice (434-449) only gates the content write on acceptVoiceSnapshot (updatedAt ordering). The press reset at line 446 runs for every snapshot, including a stale one. A dashboard or voice.state reply computed before the worker was ready arrives after the open reply with open:false. press becomes PRESS_IDLE, and when the open resolves pressOpened is a no-op, so listen.start is never sent. The hold is silently dropped and the session is open with no capture. Case B: a stale open:false arriving mid-hold means the release is never sent (pressUp is a no-op on idle), so the Host capture runs to maxTurnCaptureMs (30 s) in manual endpointing. Dashboard snapshots carry voice (http.server.ts:464), so this path is reachable on every dashboard refresh.

title: In-flight control confirmation speaks its stale turn on a reopened session's worker
scenario: executeProposal calls void runControl(proposal, speakTurn). runControl awaits agents.command (694), then calls speakAnswer with the captured old turn (698, 711 or 713). The user closes voice and reopens it before the command returns. speakAnswer (853-876) has no session-epoch or turn check: it sets state PROCESSING, then sends speak commands to whatever this.worker is now, with the current generation. The new worker plays the old confirmation text. Its playback events carry the old turn and are dropped by the turn gate (947-950), so outstanding never drains and the session sticks in PROCESSING. A stale utterance is therefore spoken in a new session. The window is the command latency, so it is narrow.

The stale line is therefore spoken in the new session. Mitigating facts that keep this from MEDIUM: pause and resume complete synchronously so their window is effectively zero; only agent.stop has a meaningful window, which requires the user to close and reopen voice within the stop latency; the spoken text is host-authored and truthful about the agent's state; the stuck PROCESSING clears on the next listenStart via bargeIn (hasSpeechInFlight). No control action is re-executed and no approval, identity or audio-retention invariant is broken, so this is a narrow stale-speech defect rather than a security-grade one. The claimed fix (an epoch check in runControl and a turn-equals-snap.turnId check in speakAnswer) is sound.

- runControl (~692-715) awaits `agents.command` (694) and then calls speakAnswer with that old turn.

The generation check does not drop them, because the generation is unchanged across close (resetAfterClose at ~303-331 keeps it).
- doOpen (~200-225) does not reset turnId. resetAfterClose sets turnId to null. The new worker's playback events carry the old turn string, so the turn gate in onWorkerEvent (~947-950) drops them. playback.started and chunk_done never reach the state machine, so the session stays in PROCESSING with outstanding > 0. A button press recovers it, because listenStart calls bargeIn when speech is in flight.

- The window is the agents.command await (http.server.ts ~418-420, a local agentCommand call, so milliseconds). The user has to close and reopen voice, which requires a new worker launch and ready wait, within that window. Practically it is narrow.

title: Playback driver calls under Speaker.gate stall the command loop and barge-in
scenario: PlayReal holds Speaker.gate (line 1653) across WaveOut.Open (1661), Submit (1663) and Out.Emit. PlayLoop calls CloseOutput (1593, under gate) and PlayReal's timeout path calls waveOut.Reset (1690, under gate). Cancel (1475-1490, waveOutReset under gate) is invoked synchronously from Dispatch (1956, speak.cancel at 2032/2259) on the single stdin thread. If a driver blocks in waveOutOpen (for example a Bluetooth profile switch on the first chunk after the 3 s idle close) or in waveOutReset, the stdin thread blocks on gate. A barge-in speak.cancel, capture.abort and shutdown then wait with no timeout for the driver, and audio keeps playing until the driver returns. The README claims speak.cancel is a synchronous reset, but nothing bounds how long that reset can take.
fix: Do not hold gate across waveOutOpen/Submit/Reset/Close. Mark the chunk and capture the handle under gate, then perform device calls outside the lock. Or run device-state changes on the playback thread and have Cancel only set flags and signal it, with a bounded wait.
why: Verified in native/voice/BunnyVoiceWorker.cs. The mechanics in the claim are accurate: Cancel holds gate (1475) across waveOut.Reset (1490); PlayReal holds gate (1653) across WaveOut.Open (1661) and Submit (1663); PlayLoop calls CloseOutput under gate (1593); the timeout path calls waveOut.Reset under gate (1690); Dispatch runs speak.cancel synchronously on the stdin thread (1956, 2032, 2259). A driver stall in waveOutOpen therefore delays Cancel's flag-marking, because Cancel cannot take gate until PlayReal releases it. The claim overstates the severity, though. Audio stops only when waveOutReset returns, and the synchronous reset on the stdin thread blocks in the same way with or without gate, so moving device calls outside the lock would not make barge-in stop audio sooner. The synchronous reset is documented design (README line 42), not a false statement. The trigger is a driver-level hang, which is not a bounded or attacker-controlled path, and no security invariant is broken by default. The honest impact is liveness and delayed chunk-marking under a device stall, which is LOW hardening. Note that the stdin-blocking and no-timeout behavior is real. Driver stall duration was not verified, as the brief specified.

Refuted as stated. Lock placement is accurate: Cancel holds gate across waveOut.Reset (BunnyVoiceWorker.cs:1475-1490), PlayReal holds gate across WaveOut.Open/Submit (1653-1670), the timeout path resets under gate (1686-1690, bounded extra 1 s wait), and PlayLoop calls CloseOutput under gate (1587-1593). But the failure scenario does not hold. (1) During a stalled waveOutOpen (1661), no output handle exists and no chunk has been submitted, so no audio is playing; the stall delays only command handling, not audio stop. Once Open returns, Submit runs under the same lock and Cancel then resets the device (1490) before the lock is released, so barge-in still stops the audio. (2) A stalled waveOutReset is the driver failing to stop playback; holding gate does not make audio play longer than the driver's own reset would. The timeout-path reset (1690) occurs only after playback has already failed to complete, so there is little audio left to keep playing. (3) Nothing in the stdin path otherwise races or deadlocks on gate, so no stale-generation or invariant violation follows. The residual concern is that the single stdin thread (Dispatch at 1956, speak.cancel at 2032, shutdown) can block on unbounded winmm driver calls while holding gate, which is a responsiveness and hardening issue depending on driver behavior that was not verified. It is at most LOW hygiene, not the MEDIUM barge-in defect claimed. Stall duration was not measured, as stated in the claim.

title: Pinned worker integrity is self-referential and checked before an await, so the exe can be swapped before spawn
scenario: verifyWorkerIntegrity (line 279) hashes bunny-voice-worker.exe and compares it to bunny-voice-worker.json, which sits in the same writable native/voice directory. The release manifest is optional (only checked if present). launchVoiceWorker then awaits outputPipe twice (285-286) before group.spawn runs the exe by path (290). A same-user process with write access to native/voice can replace the exe, and rewrite the json and manifest, in that window. The contained process then runs with mic and speaker access and the Host's env allowlist. Verification and execution are not atomic, and the pin is not anchored in the committed source.
fix: Hash the exe after the awaits and immediately before spawn, or copy the verified bytes to a private location and spawn that copy. Anchor the expected binarySha256 in committed source or the release manifest, and require the manifest rather than treating it as optional on release builds.
why:
The claim holds as stated, but its exploitability is lower than the claim suggests, so I keep MEDIUM only as a truthfulness and defense-gap finding.

title: Timed-out recognizer engine is never disposed, leaking raw-audio buffers per stuck turn
scenario: In FinalizeMain, if RecognizeCompleted does not fire within 4 s and again within 1 s after RecognizeAsyncCancel, done stays false (1301) and engine.Dispose() is skipped (1317-1320). The SpeechRecognitionEngine, its event closures and the CaptureTurn with PcmPipe are then still referenced by SAPI. PcmPipe's buffer holds up to roughly 1 MB of raw microphone PCM (960 KB max turn plus 9600 bytes of padding) and is never zeroed. Nothing caps how many such engines accumulate. A recognizer that repeatedly hangs on a turn grows memory per turn for the life of the process, and the raw speech stays in memory.
fix: Dispose the engine on a timeout path too, or keep a bounded count of abandoned engines and fail new captures with STT_UNAVAILABLE beyond it. Zero the PcmPipe buffer when the turn finalizes.
why: The defect holds as stated, with one qualifier. BunnyVoiceWorker.cs:1296-1301 leaves done=false when RecognizeCompleted does not fire within 4 s and again within 1 s after RecognizeAsyncCancel. The finally block at 1317-1320 then skips engine.Dispose(). Nothing else disposes the engine: a grep for Dispose and engine finds no other call. Program.Active is cleared at 1238 by the capture thread, so a new capture.start is accepted while the stuck engine is still unreleased, and nothing caps how many such engines accumulate. The worker is a long-lived stdin command loop, so the growth is per hung turn for the life of the process. PcmPipe (815-856) holds unread PCM in buf; the buffer doubles at 846 and is never cleared, and per-turn audio is bounded by maxMs (<=30000 ms, 960,000 bytes, from StartCapture). The skeptic checks that could refute it do not hold. Line numbers match. The claim that SAPI still holds references is unverified, because I cannot run the worker, so the exact retention mechanism is an assumption; the leak itself is real without it, because nothing disposes the engine on that path. Severity stays MEDIUM: it needs a recognizer hang on the timeout path, the impact is about 1 MB of raw PCM per occurrence, and no invariant is broken by default. Not verified: whether System.Speech finalizers reclaim the engine, which would bound the leak in practice. Read-only review; nothing was executed.

The claim holds in its core facts, with the severity left at MEDIUM. Evidence from native/voice/BunnyVoiceWorker.cs:

- engine.Dispose() is only reached inside finally under `if (done && engine != null)` (~1317-1319). On the not-done path the engine is never disposed, and no other code disposes it (grep for Dispose shows only that call site and the worker shutdown path, which only handles Active).

Each new turn after a stuck one creates a fresh SpeechRecognitionEngine (StartRecognizer, ~1090), so a recognizer that hangs on every turn accumulates one engine plus its PcmPipe per turn for the process lifetime.
- PcmPipe (815-850) grows buf by doubling and never shrinks or zeroes it. Max turn is maxMs capped at 30000 (2162-2164) times BytesPerMs 32 = 960,000 bytes (2187), plus the 9,600-byte pad. Capacity can reach roughly 1 to 2 MB, consistent with the claim's order of magnitude. Raw PCM is retained only in process memory, not disk, logs or events.

Limits on the claim: it needs a recognizer hang on each turn, so the trigger is abnormal and not attacker-controlled; the impact is memory growth and raw-audio residence in process memory, not a security bypass. Zeroing the buffer is not the leak's root cause (it applies to the normal path too). The claim's "still referenced by SAPI" is not directly proven by code and was not verified at runtime. MEDIUM fits "defense gap with limited impact" under the bounded-buffers invariant.

title: Each speak.cancel spawns an unbounded background thread
scenario: CancelSpeech creates a new Thread for every speak.cancel that runs PollRenderSilence for up to 1 s. There is no cap or coalescing, so a burst of cancel commands creates a matching burst of short-lived threads. This is not bounded in the way the 'bounded queues everywhere' invariant asks for.

However, the claimed burst is not reachable. The only host senders of speak.cancel are voice-session.server.ts:291 (close(), gated on wasSpeaking) and :885 (bargeIn()). bargeIn() is only invoked when hasSpeechInFlight(state) (SPEAKING/PROCESSING) or snap.playing is true (lines 344, 395, 415, 434). Each bargeIn sets playing=false and transitions the FSM to INTERRUPTED (lines 879-897), and INTERRUPTED is not in flight (voice-fsm.ts:70-72). So a further cancel requires a new speak command to put the FSM back into SPEAKING/PROCESSING, and each speak originates from a fresh turn/LLM chunk. Cancel rate is therefore bounded by user-driven turns, and each thread lives at most ~1 s, so the number of live meter threads stays small in practice. The missing cap is at most a hardening nit (a threads-not-queues concern rather than a buffer or invariant break), and the "bounded queues everywhere" invariant concerns buffers and queues, which this code does not use. No exploitable or realistic-condition defect was found; I did not run anything.

Not verified: that the Host never retries speak.cancel in a tight loop on transport error (tryWorker path at voice-session.server.ts was not fully traced).

title: Device index from the command wraps silently through a (int) cast
scenario: int device = (int)Num(cmd, 'device', -1) truncates a 64-bit value without a range check. A device value of 4294967296 becomes 0, so capture silently opens device 0 and speak plays on device 0, rather than the command being rejected. Input comes only from the Host, so this is a hardening issue, not an exploit.
fix: Reject device values outside [-1, int.MaxValue] or any value that does not fit an int, and report INTERNAL or DEVICE_UNAVAILABLE.
why: Mechanism confirmed as claimed. native/voice/BunnyVoiceWorker.cs:2063-2072 (Num) returns any double within long range unchanged, so 4294967296 passes through as a long. Line 2160 (StartCapture) and 2241 (Speak) then apply an unchecked (int) cast; scripts/build-voice-worker.mjs invokes csc.exe with no /checked flag, so the value wraps to 0. Line 2226 bounds only against waveInGetNumDevs(), and 0 passes that check when a device exists, so capture opens device 0 silently. The claim's line numbers and premise are accurate. Mitigating context: the only input is stdin from the Host (line 1938), and the Host hardcodes device: -1 at src/lib/bunny-host/voice/voice-session.server.ts:363 (capture.start) and :796 (speak), so the wrap is unreachable from shipped code without changing the Host or compromising the Host-to-worker channel. The reported device index in capture.started comes from the actually-opened device (info.Index = device), so there is no misreport. Remaining impact is hardening only; LOW is the right severity. Suggested fix stands: reject device outside [-1, int.MaxValue] with INTERNAL or DEVICE_UNAVAILABLE at parse time.

It is still a real input-validation gap that silently changes behavior instead of failing with DEVICE_UNAVAILABLE, as the claim's fix suggests. Not a BLOCKER or HIGH under the rubric.

title: Unguarded non-VoiceFault exception on playback or finalize threads kills the whole worker process
scenario: PlayLoop calls PlayReal/PlayNull with only VoiceFault caught (1665). Out.Emit (1634, 1672, 1702) is not guarded, and an IOException from a closed stdout or any other exception from WaveOut.Open/Submit escapes the background thread. On .NET Framework an unhandled background-thread exception terminates the process with no error event and no bye. The tail of FinalizeMain after its try (1323-1339) has the same issue. The failure is fail-closed and the job kill still applies, but the process exits without a diagnostic.
fix: Wrap the PlayLoop body and the FinalizeMain tail in catch-all handlers that emit a bounded error event and fail the current chunk or turn only.
why: Claim holds in substance; severity LOW is correct. Evidence from native/voice/BunnyVoiceWorker.cs: PlayLoop (line ~1582) runs on a background thread (line 1422-1423, IsBackground=true) with no try/catch around the body. The call at ~1605 (`bool ok = nullOutput ? PlayNull(c) : PlayReal(c);`) is unguarded. PlayReal's only handler is `catch (VoiceFault f)` (~1665); Out.Emit (Out.cs:227, unguarded stream.Write/Flush on stdout) is called inside PlayNull/PlayReal under gate, so an IOException from a closed stdout escapes. WaveOut.Open throws VoiceFault for mmsystem errors (line ~754), so the non-VoiceFault risk is limited to stdout I/O, P/Invoke failures, or marshalling errors. Main (line 1842) has no AppDomain.UnhandledException handler (grep finds none), so an escaping background-thread exception terminates the process. FinalizeMain's trailing lock block (~1323-1339) sits outside the try at ~1313 and has the same exposure, and the same applies to Out.Emit calls in other threads. Impact: the process dies without a bye or error event. Fail-closed behavior holds and the F04 Job Object kill still applies, so no invariant (no execution authority, no raw audio retention, no uncontained fallback) is broken. This is a hardening and diagnostic gap only, which matches the rubric's LOW. Not verified: how the host classifies an unexpected worker exit, and whether a Windows crash dump could contain PCM buffers (out of scope for this claim). Read-only review; no tests or audio were run.

title: Finalize decision can read stale onset state and drop recognized speech
scenario: FinalizeMain joins the capture thread for at most 2000 ms (1286), then reads sawOnset and highEnergy under gate (1327). sawOnset is written only in CaptureLoop's finally (1233). If the capture thread is still blocked (for example in Out.Emit under stdout backpressure) past the 2 s join, sawOnset is still false. StopDecision then returns no_speech or noise_only, and texts recognized during the turn are discarded. The result is a truthfulness defect under stdout stall, not a privacy leak.
fix: Publish sawOnset and highEnergy as they change (under gate) rather than only in the capture thread's finally, or wait for the capture thread to finish before deciding.
why: The claim holds as stated, and I could not refute it. Recognized texts are then not emitted as stt.final (lines 1328-1338). The only way the capture thread can block that long is Out.Emit (line 227-241) stalling on the stdout write under Lock, because PcmPipe.Push (lines 823-848) never blocks; it grows its buffer. So the scenario needs a stdout stall of more than 2 s from the Host. The effect is a truthfulness defect: a real utterance is reported as no_speech, and the worker fails closed with no text promoted and no authority change. That fits the rubric's LOW for a hardening-level truthfulness issue. The claimed fix (publish onset/high-energy state under gate as it changes, or join the capture thread to completion before deciding) is sound.

title: Build skip-check ignores compiler, flags and System.Speech hashes
scenario: The up-to-date check at lines 36-44 compares only sourceSha256 and binarySha256 to the existing record. If csc.exe, the compiler flags or the System.Speech reference change, the script returns the prior record unchanged (line 41). That record keeps the old compiler.sha256, version and systemSpeech.sha256, so the build record can describe a toolchain that did not produce the current binary.

The code at scripts/build-voice-worker.mjs:36-44 does skip on sourceSha256 and binarySha256 only, and the flags (line 47) and compiler/speech hashes are not part of the skip key. But the record it returns is still truthful about the current binary. The skip fires only when sha(output) equals prior.binarySha256, so the on-disk exe is byte-identical to the one the prior record's build produced. That build's compiler.sha256, version and systemSpeech.sha256 are therefore the toolchain that produced the current binary. The claimed "record describes a toolchain that did not produce the current binary" does not follow. The record also never states the compiler flags, so no flag claim is falsified. The only real effect is that a changed csc.exe, speech DLL or flag set (line 47) does not trigger a rebuild, so the binary may not reflect the current build settings. That is at most a freshness/hardening nit, not a truthfulness defect or an invariant break, so it does not meet the rubric's LOW threshold as a defect in the record. The sha binding on binarySha256 that the runtime relies on is intact. Verified by reading lines 32-76 only; no builds or executions were run.

title: Worker exit or poll failure drops the worker reference without closing its job group
scenario: VoiceSessionManager.onWorkerExit (1058-1067) sets this.worker = null and sets WORKER_EXITED but never calls worker.close(). title: WPF Mute button cannot mute the microphone
scenario: User clicks Mute while unmuted. The WPF client sends voice.mute with { muted: true }. The Host reads data.on === true (http.server.ts:1159), so it calls mute(false). The microphone keeps capturing, and the label truthfully stays 'Mute', so the control is silently a no-op. The same click while muted would unmute, so the button behaves inverted in one direction and dead in the other.
fix: Send @{ on = (-not [bool]$snap.muted) } in the WPF mute handler and add a contract test for the key name.
why:
The claim holds exactly as stated; I could not refute it. Evidence:
- install/Bunny-Island.Voice.ps1:423 sends `Add-BunnyVoiceRequest 'voice.mute' @{ muted = (-not [bool]$snap.muted) } $true`. The WPF key is `muted`.
- Add-BunnyVoiceRequest (Voice.ps1:66-70) and New-BunnyVoiceRequestMessage (Voice.ps1:58-64) serialize `data` unchanged, with no key translation, so the Host receives `{ muted: ... }`.
- src/lib/bunny-host/http.server.ts:1158-1159 reads only `data.on === true`, so a `muted` key always yields mute(false).
- Result: clicking Mute while unmuted sends muted:true, which the Host reads as on=false, so mute(false) is a no-op. Clicking while muted sends muted:false, which unmutes. The label is driven by snap.muted (Voice.ps1:324), so it stays truthfully "Mute". The button is dead in one direction and inverted in the other.
- The desktop path is correct: src/store/use-island.ts:834 sends { on }. The Host test voice-host.test.ts:163 only exercises on:false, so no contract test catches the key mismatch.
Severity is MEDIUM rather than higher: this is a broken user-facing microphone-mute control, not a listed security invariant. The label is truthful, and the desktop and hotkey paths still reach the same Host route with the correct key. Fix as the claim suggests: send `@{ on = (-not [bool]$snap.muted) }` and add a contract test pinning the `on` key.

Claim holds as stated. Evidence: install/Bunny-Island.Voice.ps1:423 sends `Add-BunnyVoiceRequest 'voice.mute' @{ muted = (-not [bool]$snap.muted) }`. The request body is serialized as-is (New-BunnyVoiceRequestMessage, Voice.ps1:58-62, no key translation). src/lib/bunny-host/http.server.ts:1158-1159 reads `voice.mute(data.on === true)`, so `data.on` is undefined and the call is always mute(false). Clicking Mute while unmuted is a no-op; clicking while muted unmutes. The desktop path (src/store/use-island.ts:834) sends `{ on }`, so only the WPF client is broken. The contract test (voice-host.test.ts:163) uses `{ on: false }`, so the mismatch is not caught by tests. Nuance: the claim's "inverted" wording is slightly off. The button is dead in the mute direction and works only in the unmute direction. The label stays truthful ("Mute" remains shown, since snap.muted never changes), so no state is misrepresented. Impact is a defective privacy control with a visible failure, which fits MEDIUM as a truthfulness/defense-gap issue rather than HIGH. Recommended fix matches the claim: send `@{ on = (-not [bool]$snap.muted) }` and add a contract test for the key name.

title: WPF quick tap leaves the mic open for up to 30 s with no release
scenario: A press shorter than 350 ms calls Start-BunnyVoicePointer, which sends listen.start with source 'push_to_talk'. The Host maps that to manual endpointing (voice-session.server.ts:364) and Stop-BunnyVoicePointer sends no listen.end for a tap. The worker never finishes on VAD, so capture runs to maxTurnCaptureMs (30000) and ends with reason 'max' (BunnyVoiceWorker.cs:1218). The UI shows 'Listening' for ~30 s after the user apparently released, and the captured audio is then transcribed and routed. The comment at line 199 says a tap is left to VAD, which is false.
fix: Send a non-manual source for taps (or always send listen.end on pointer up and let the Host decide), and correct the comment to match the actual behaviour.
why:
The claim holds on the code path as stated; I could not refute it.

Path traced:
- install/Bunny-Island.Voice.ps1:192-196: Start-BunnyVoicePointer calls Start-BunnyVoiceListen 'push_to_talk' on every mouse press, with no hold threshold.
- install/Bunny-Island.Voice.ps1:198-200: Stop-BunnyVoicePointer calls Stop-BunnyVoiceListen only when the hold is >= 350 ms. A quick tap sends no voice.listen.end. The comment at line 199 ("a quick tap leaves the turn to voice activity detection") is false.
- install/Bunny-Island.Voice.ps1:202-210 (Invoke-BunnyVoiceClick): the Click handler returns early inside the 500 ms mouse guard, so a tap does not end the capture through that path either.
- src/lib/bunny-host/voice/voice-session.server.ts:364: endpointing is "manual" for source push_to_talk. Line 367 arms the idle timer only for hands_free, so no Host timer ends a push_to_talk tap.
- native/voice/BunnyVoiceWorker.cs:1193/1198: Finish("vad") is gated on VadEndpoint, which is false in manual mode, so the worker never finishes on speech end or silence.
- native/voice/BunnyVoiceWorker.cs:1216-1218: capture only ends at MaxBytes, which is 30 s via voice-protocol.ts:234. Finish("max") is the only exit.

So a tap leaves the mic capturing for up to 30 s with the UI in a listening state, and the audio is then processed as a normal turn. Mitigations (the user can press again, which aborts and restarts capture, and the state is visible on screen) limit the impact, which supports MEDIUM rather than HIGH. The false comment at line 199 is a truthfulness defect. Line numbers match the claim, except the source mapping at http.server.ts:1140 is inside voiceCommand around 1128-1131; this does not change the finding.

The claim holds as stated; I could not refute it. Evidence chain, all read from the working tree:

1. install/Bunny-Island.Voice.ps1:15 sets $bunnyVoiceHoldMs = 350. Line 192-194 (Start-BunnyVoicePointer) sends voice.listen.start with source 'push_to_talk' on PreviewMouseLeftButtonDown (line 416). Line 198-200 (Stop-BunnyVoicePointer) only calls Stop-BunnyVoiceListen when the hold is >= 350 ms, so a tap sends no voice.listen.end. Line 199 comment ("a quick tap leaves the turn to voice activity detection") is false for this path. Invoke-BunnyVoiceClick (line 184-190) returns early within 500 ms of a mouse press, so it does not compensate.

2. src/lib/bunny-host/voice/voice-session.server.ts:364 sets endpointing to 'manual' when source === 'push_to_talk'. The only other capture-end paths are an explicit capture.end (listenEnd, line ~380) and the hands-free idle timer (armIdle, only for hands_free mode, line 367). Neither applies to a push_to_talk tap.

3. native/voice/BunnyVoiceWorker.cs:2161 defaults endpointing to 'manual' and line 2187 sets VadEndpoint only when endpointing == "vad". The VAD-driven Finish("vad") at ~line 1190 is gated on VadEndpoint, so a manual capture never finishes on silence. Capture ends only at maxMs (30000 per voice-protocol.ts:234 and the Host's maxTurnCaptureMs) via Finish("max") at line 1218, or on an explicit end or abort.

Severity: I agree with MEDIUM. The defect is a truthfulness bug (a false code comment and a UI state that does not match the user's release) plus an unintended open microphone for up to 30 s. The 30 s of captured audio is not retained, and the claim's downstream routing (auto-admission only for local tool-free generations) limits impact. It does not break a listed invariant outright. I did not confirm the exact downstream behaviour on 'max' finish beyond the claim's own description, since the host-side transcription path was not traced in full. The hotkey path is not affected because it uses source 'hotkey' and therefore VAD endpointing.

title: Desktop hold-to-talk ends on silence while held, but the button still says Listening
scenario: Desktop listen.start is sent without a source, so the Host defaults to 'button' and uses VAD endpointing. The user holds the button, speaks, pauses about 900 ms after speech onset, and the worker finishes capture (reason 'vad'). The Host moves to TRANSCRIBING ('Finishing your words…'), but the button keeps reading 'Listening… release to finish' because the label is bound to store.voicePressing, which is set on pointer down (and during open/ARMING, before capture.started), not to capture truth. Speech after the cut-off is never captured, and the eventual release's listen.end is ignored because the turn is no longer LISTENING.
fix: Send source 'push_to_talk' (manual endpointing) for hold-to-talk, and derive the 'Listening… release to finish' label from snapshot.capturing rather than from the press flag alone.
why: Claim verified as stated. (1) src/store/use-island.ts:461 sends `voice.listen.start` with no data, so http.server.ts:1152-1153 passes `source(undefined)`, which falls back to "button" (the source() helper maps anything not hotkey/push_to_talk/hands_free to "button"). (2) voice-session.server.ts:364 sets `endpointing: source === "push_to_talk" ? "manual" : "vad"`, so desktop hold-to-talk runs VAD endpointing. (3) BunnyVoiceWorker.cs around lines 1190-1198: on vad speech_end or no_speech, `if (VadEndpoint) Finish("vad")` fires during a held press. (4) Host then gets capture.stopped and sets TRANSCRIBING (voice-session.server.ts:~985, 'capture.stopped' case), and listenEnd (voice-session.server.ts ~397-400) only acts when state is LISTENING, so the later release is dropped. (5) voice.tsx:80 and :164 bind the label to store.voicePressing (= press.pressed from voice-press.ts), which stays true until pointer-up, so the button keeps reading "Listening… release to finish" while no capture is running. The mechanism is real and the consequence (speech after the VAD cut is lost, and the UI misstates capture state) matches the claimed scenario. Nuance: the claimed "900 ms after onset" is imprecise (the architecture doc says >=900 ms silence AND >=700 ms without new hypothesis), but the mechanism is unchanged. Severity MEDIUM fits the rubric: a truthfulness defect with limited impact, since the user can still release and retry, and nothing unauthorized or unsafe happens. Architecture doc (test-results/ma3/t10/voice-architecture.md:32) describes the button as "press-and-hold", which supports the view that hold should be manual endpointing. Suggested fix is sound: send source push_to_talk for the button, and derive the label from snapshot.capturing.

title: Answer route attribution is stale or misattributed
scenario: (a) A spoken chat turn is answered by ollama, then the user types 'how many agents are running?'. The host-facts answer shows 'From Bunny facts' together with the old 'Answered by ollama · <model>' line, because acceptFinal (474-479) and text() never clear route; only listenStart (355) does. (b) A hosted or tool-capable task is refused with TOOLS_TEXT, but route is assigned at 738 before the refusal branch, so the UI shows 'Not done by voice' with 'Answered by <provider> · <model>' even though no model answered. The desktop routeLabel and WPF route line both display whatever route is present.
fix: Set route only when a model answer is actually produced, and clear route at the start of every turn in acceptFinal, text() and controlConfirm.
why:
Claim verified as stated, both halves, by reading the code.

(a) Stale route on later turns: src/lib/bunny-host/voice/voice-session.server.ts sets snap.route only at line 738 (inside chat()). The only resets are the initial null at line 150 and listenStart at line 355. text() (426-446) calls acceptFinal (474) directly, and acceptFinal (474-479) never clears route. onFinal (503-520) also goes through acceptFinal. Host-facts answers are rendered in src/components/island/voice.tsx:189-193 whenever voice.answer is set and routeLabel(voice.route) is non-null, so a typed "how many agents are running?" after a spoken Ollama turn shows "From Bunny facts" followed by "Answered by ollama · <model>". routeLabel (voice-model.ts:144-148) returns the label for any non-null route, and the WPF line at install/Bunny-Island.Voice.ps1:301 does the same.

(b) Route set before refusal: at 738-742 the route is assigned from the chat task before the check at 744-746. When task.state !== "waiting_for_approval" || task.hasMission || !task.mayLaunch, or chat.admit throws (749-752), speakAnswer(TOOLS_TEXT, "refusal") runs with the route already set. The UI then shows "Not done by voice" (voice-model.ts:158) together with "Answered by <provider> · <model>" even though no model produced an answer. The label asserts an answer that did not happen.

Impact is display-only: no authority, approval or agent control changes, and the route is not used for any gating decision. That is a truthfulness defect with limited impact, which fits MEDIUM under the rubric. The claim's line numbers and quoted code match the source.

The claim holds on both sub-points as stated, verified by reading code (read-only, nothing run).

title: Level meter freshness is measured on poll receipt, not on the level's own timestamp
scenario: levelBars checks now - receivedAt (poll time) instead of level.at. If the worker stops emitting level events while capturing stays true (a stalled or hung capture loop, which no Host-side deadline catches in push-to-talk mode since armIdle only runs for hands-free), each poll keeps receipt fresh and the bars hold the last RMS value indefinitely while the status reads 'Listening…'. The WPF client does check level.at (Bunny-Island.Voice.ps1:279), so the desktop meter is weaker than the native one.
fix: Require now - snapshot.level.at < VOICE_FRESH_MS (as WPF does) before showing any non-zero bar.
why:
The claim holds as stated, with the impact limited to a truthfulness defect in the level meter. Evidence:
- src/components/island/voice-model.ts:134 gates bars on `now - receivedAt > VOICE_FRESH_MS`, not `level.at`. The store sets `voiceReceivedAt = Date.now()` on every poll (src/store/use-island.ts:439), so receipt stays fresh while the Host snapshot is unchanged.
- The Host keeps `snap.level` set until a state transition clears it (voice-session.server.ts:963 sets it only on a worker "level" event; it is cleared at 356, 401, 417, 984, 990, 1051, 1064, 1099, 1186). There is no age-based clearing of level on the Host.
- The WPF client does check level age: install/Bunny-Island.Voice.ps1:279 requires `($now - $snap.level.at) -lt $bunnyVoiceFreshMs`. The claim's citation is accurate.
- armIdle (voice-session.server.ts:1178-1191) runs only for hands-free, as claimed.
- Refinement: listenStart passes `maxMs: VOICE_LIMITS.maxTurnCaptureMs` to the worker (voice-session.server.ts:365). That deadline is enforced worker-side only, so a hung worker would not honor it. The Host therefore has no backstop in push-to-talk mode, which supports the claim.
- Not verified: the BunnyVoiceWorker.cs:1206-1210 emission details, which I did not read.
Impact is cosmetic: the status text still derives from open/capturing plus receipt time (voice-model.ts:69), so the label is not a security or authority issue. The bars can misrepresent a stalled capture as live input. The proposed fix (require `now - level.at < VOICE_FRESH_MS`, matching WPF) is sound on the same machine, where host epoch and client Date.now() share a clock.

The defect is real as stated, and the claim understates its scope. Verified facts:

1. src/components/island/voice-model.ts:134 gates the bars on `now - receivedAt > VOICE_FRESH_MS`, where receivedAt is the client poll time. It never checks `level.at`. So a stale snapshot.level keeps the bars non-zero as long as polls arrive.

2. src/lib/bunny-host/voice/voice-session.server.ts:962-963 sets `snap.level.at = this.now()` (Host receipt time of the last worker "level" event). The value is not cleared unless some other event clears it (lines 984, 990, 1051, 1064, 1099, 1186). Nothing in the Host expires it, so the last RMS value persists.

3. Worker side: native/voice/BunnyVoiceWorker.cs:1211 emits "level" only every 5 frames while capturing. A device or capture-thread stall that produces no frames stops emitting levels while capturing stays true.

4. Host-side capture deadlines: voice-session.server.ts:365 sends maxMs=maxTurnCaptureMs (30 s) to the worker, but the Host itself never sets a timer for push-to-talk. armIdle (line 1178) runs only for hands-free. So in push-to-talk nothing on the Host ends a hung capture.

5. The scope is wider than the meter. voice-model.ts:69 (voiceListening) also uses `now - receivedAt < VOICE_FRESH_MS`, so the "Listening…" status label (voice-model.ts:~105) stays true with the same root cause. The claim mentions this only indirectly.

Severity: this is a UI truthfulness defect (the status says the mic is capturing when it is not). It does not touch agent control, approvals, audio retention or the execution path, so it is limited in impact. The rubric puts truthfulness defects with limited impact at MEDIUM, above the LOW the claim proposed. The claim's fix is correct: check `snapshot.level.at` against VOICE_FRESH_MS, which is valid because both timestamps are Host epoch milliseconds (voice-protocol.ts:174). Note that Bunny-Island.Voice.ps1:279 already does this check, which confirms the WPF path is the intended behaviour.

title: Speaking state and Interrupt are not freshness-gated
scenario: voiceSpeaking() returns snapshot.playing with no freshness check, and controls.interrupt uses it. If the Host stops answering mid-playback, the panel correctly shows 'Reconnecting…', but Interrupt stays enabled and the orb (voice.tsx:79-82) keeps the 'working' breathing animation indefinitely. WPF does the same (Bunny-Island.Voice.ps1:322).
fix: Gate speaking and interrupt on the same freshness check used for listening (receivedAt within VOICE_STALE_MS).
why:
The claim holds as stated, with a caveat on the proposed fix.

Verified in code:
- src/components/island/voice-model.ts:73-75: voiceSpeaking() returns snapshot.playing with no receivedAt or VOICE_STALE_MS check.
- voice-model.ts:260: interrupt = available && open && (voiceSpeaking(snapshot) || state === "PROCESSING"). The `stale` value computed at line 247 is used only for pushToTalk (line 259), not interrupt.
- voice.tsx:79: orb = live ? "listening" : ... : speaking ? "working" : "idle". `live` (line 71) is freshness-gated, `speaking` (line 72) is not, so the orb shows "working" while the status line reads "Reconnecting…" (voiceStatus returns that label first, voice-model.ts:92-93).
- voice.tsx:82 and :237: bargeIn and the Interrupt button's disabled state use the non-fresh speaking flag.
- Bunny-Island.Voice.ps1:322: VoiceInterrupt.IsEnabled = $online -and $open -and [bool]$snap.playing, with no $Fresh check, even though the label at line 218 uses $Fresh.
- use-island.ts:438-439 only overwrites voice on a successful reply, so the last "playing: true" snapshot persists during an outage.

Why the severity stays LOW: no security invariant is broken. The label is honest, since "Reconnecting…" is shown. The only defect is that the orb animation implies speaking from a stale snapshot. Interrupt also cannot reach a Host that has stopped answering, so the click is a no-op and does not stop audio either way.

Caveat on the proposed fix: gating Interrupt on freshness would disable the only visible stop control during exactly the window where worker audio may still be playing and the Host is slow. That is the wrong direction. The better fix is to keep Interrupt enabled and gate only the orb's "working" state (and the bargeIn copy) on freshness. The same applies to the WPF line 322.

The defect holds as stated, with a caveat on the proposed fix. Evidence: voice-model.ts:73-75 returns snapshot.playing with no receivedAt check. voice-model.ts:260 makes interrupt enabled whenever available && open && voiceSpeaking(snapshot), with no freshness term. voice.tsx:79 maps speaking to orb "working" when live is false, and voice.tsx:82 uses speaking in bargeIn. Nothing clears a held snapshot on a stale poll: use-island.ts:436-439 only replaces voice on new answers, and the last playing=true snapshot persists while the Host is silent. So during "Reconnecting…" (voiceStatus at voice-model.ts:92-93, which does come first) the orb keeps the working animation and Interrupt stays enabled. This is a truthfulness and visual defect only. No invariant is broken: the status line is correct, and no authority or audio retention is affected. The stated fix is not safe to apply as written. Gating interrupt on freshness would disable the only in-panel stop control while the worker may still be playing audio after a Host hiccup, which runs against the barge-in invariant. The orb can be fixed on its own, and interrupt should stay fail-open. The WPF comparison is weaker than claimed. Bunny-Island.Voice.ps1:322 gates on $online, $open and snap.playing, and $online probably already reflects Host reachability, so WPF may not behave the same way. I did not verify $online's definition. Severity LOW is the right rubric level.

title: Resume is acknowledged on a weaker check than pause or stop
scenario: For agent.resume, runControl treats the command as confirmed whenever the row is neither PAUSED nor terminal. If the resume is accepted but the agent lands in another non-paused state such as WAITING_FOR_USER, Bunny says '<agent> is resumed.' That is an acknowledgement not backed by the canonical state the spec requires.
fix: Require the expected canonical state (RUNNING, or the state the agent should reach) for resume, and otherwise use the 'I'm not sure it changed' copy.
why: Claim does not hold as stated. voice-session.server.ts:53-75 (runControl) reads the row from the canonical agents.rows() snapshot after agents.command resolves, so the acknowledgement is backed by canonical state, which is what the invariant requires. For agent.resume, the check (row.state !== "PAUSED" && !isTerminalAgent(row.state), lines 68-69) confirms that the agent left PAUSED. agent-runtime.server.ts:225-247 shows resume only succeeds once the hold is lifted (pausedAt cleared, run reopened), and it refuses (throws CommandRefusedError) otherwise, so a successful resume really did resume. The claim's stated premise that the acknowledgement is "not backed by canonical state" is incorrect. The only residual gap is precision: "X is resumed." can be spoken when the post-resume state is WAITING_FOR_USER. That is a copy-precision nit at most (LOW hardening), not an unbacked acknowledgement or an invariant break, and the claim's severity and fix do not follow from the evidence. Pause and stop are checked against their exact target states, so resume is the only asymmetric case, but this does not rise to a defect as claimed.

Refutation of the claim that resume is acknowledged on a weaker check than the spec requires.

What holds: voice-session.server.ts:701-708 reads the row from the canonical runtime after the command, and for agent.resume the confirmed expression is row.state !== "PAUSED" && !isTerminalAgent(row.state). The claim describes this accurately, and the else branch (line 713) uses the "I'm not sure it changed" copy.

What does not hold: the claim says the spec requires the expected canonical state (RUNNING) for resume. The architecture doc (test-results/ma3/t10/voice-architecture.md:51) says only that "Bunny acknowledges only the canonical post-state", and the post-state is what is read here. Pause and stop are checked against their exact target state, but resume's target is not a single state. agent-runtime.server.ts:216-245 shows resume can legitimately leave the agent outside RUNNING: it can require fresh scope consent (WAITING_FOR_USER, lines 226-231), and reissueStaleAgenticRequests (line 245) can reissue asks after the hold lifts. Requiring RUNNING would therefore make Bunny wrongly say "not sure it changed" in those cases. The "resumed" wording is also literally true, because the pause flag was cleared (line 239).

Residual nit (not a defect under the rubric): a user can hear "<agent> is resumed." while the agent sits in WAITING_FOR_USER awaiting an on-screen consent. A more precise message would help, but no invariant is broken and nothing unsafe follows.

title: Intent sequence is not scoped to the Host epoch
scenario: uiSeq starts at 0 in each VoiceSessionManager (voice-session.server.ts:117). After a Host restart the new Host emits seq 1, 2, ... while the page keeps its old voiceSeen (and the WPF client keeps bunnyVoiceUiSeen). Any intent with seq at or below the old value is silently dropped, so the expected agentic-sheet navigation does not happen until the new seq passes the old one.
fix: Reset the seen seq whenever hostEpoch changes (or include the epoch in the seen key).
why: Claim holds as stated, with corrected locations. The page-side dedupe is in src/store/use-island.ts:424/440-441: `voiceSeen` is module state that is only reset to null on its own, and acceptVoice() calls planUiIntent(next.uiIntent, voiceSeen) with no hostEpoch comparison, even though acceptVoiceSnapshot() at voice-model.ts:320 does treat an epoch change as a reset. planUiIntent (voice-model.ts:302-305) drops any intent with seq <= seen. The WPF side has the same shape: Bunny-Island.Voice.ps1:143-145 compares $seq against $script:bunnyVoiceUiSeen and never checks the epoch. The Host side is confirmed: uiSeq is a per-manager counter starting at 0 (voice-session.server.ts:117) and is incremented at :1226 without any epoch offset, so a restarted Host emits seq 1, 2, ... The failure is real: after a Host restart with the page still open, navigation intents with seq at or below the old high-water mark are silently dropped until the new seq passes it. Impact is limited to agentic-sheet navigation (ui focus), not to any execution, approval, identity, audio, or agent-control invariant, so LOW matches the rubric. Suggested fix is the claim's: reset the seen seq on hostEpoch change in use-island.ts and in the WPF script.

The defect is real but narrow, and the claim's location is imprecise. Verified by reading code only.

Mechanics confirmed:
